Subject: Private Offer: pricing and buyer approval path for AcmeCloud

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the product overview yesterday — the latency and cost numbers look promising. We're starting to scope an AWS Marketplace private offer (seller-guided) for a 36-month enterprise contract and need to understand a few things before we loop in procurement: 

1) Pricing bands: what discount ranges do you typically allow on a 36-month private offer vs. standard list? Any guardrails around minimums for co-sell approval?
2) Term-related concessions: do you have recommended term-to-discount tradeoffs (12 / 24 / 36) that work inside the marketplace flow?
3) Buyer approval lanes: our procurement org requires a buyer-approval ladder — who needs to sign in AWS Marketplace for private offers, and do we need an internal Acme approval before you submit the private offer?
4) Marketplace fees / surcharges: any items that I'll need to flag to our finance team?

Can you send a quick mutual action plan so we can align legal/procurement watchers? I'm copying our procurement lead (procure@acmecloud.com) and Suresh in product to keep them in the loop.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Greene
Head of Cloud Partnerships
AcmeCloud

Hi Paul — great to meet yesterday, and thanks for the clear list of asks. High level answers below; Vanessa (Marketplace & Partner Ops) is cc'd and will add process-level details. I'll attach a short mutual action plan and a term matrix for Acme to share with procurement.

Short answers:
- Pricing bands: For a 36-month private offer we generally approve deeper discounts because of the long-term commitment — typical range is 25–35% off list for enterprise-scale usage. Exceptions (deeper discounts) require Partner Ops + Sales leadership signoff and a co-sell commitment.
- Term tradeoffs: 12mo = standard; 24mo = ~5–8% extra discount; 36mo = additional 5–10% on top of 24mo band depending on committed ARR and forecast accuracy. We'll surface exact numbers in the attached term matrix.
- Buyer approval lanes: Two parallel approvals are common: (a) Acme internal procurement signoff, and (b) AWS Marketplace private-offer acceptance by Redwood (we submit the offer into the buyer's AWS console). For co-sell where AWS rebate/credits are involved, we also need AWS Partner Business approval — Partner Ops will coordinate that step.
- Marketplace fees: AWS takes its marketplace standard fees (list), which we factor into net pricing in the matrix. There are also seller-initiated marketplace fee pass-throughs for certain metered components; we'll call that out.

Attached: RDW-Acme-Mutual-Action-Plan-v1.xlsx (MAP) and acme-po-term-matrix.csv.

Next steps:
1) Vanessa will outline the approval sequence and what she needs from Acme (PO, billing info, authorized buyer emails).
2) If you want a formal seller-guided private offer, we can draft an initial offer for your review and route to your procurement for signature.

—

Hi Paul — thanks for looping us in. Quick operational notes for Acme's procurement team to expedite a seller-guided private offer on AWS Marketplace: 

1) Required buyer-side inputs (provided by Acme):
   - Authorized buyer email(s) in the AWS account (one to accept the private offer)
   - Purchase order number or PO-format details (if your SOW requires it)
   - Billing contact + tax information

2) Redwood steps (what we'll do):
   - Create draft private offer in AWS Seller Central with the agreed term, price bands, and marketplace SKUs.
   - Send private offer link to the authorized buyer email for acceptance. Once accepted, AWS issues the marketplace transaction and we invoice per the offer terms.

3) Approval lanes and timing:
   - Internal Acme approval: typical procurement signoff (1–3 business days depending on org).
   - Redwood approval: Partner Ops validates pricing bands against our discount policy (we'll turn around approvals in 24–48 hours for standard bands; exceptions routed to Sales leadership).
   - AWS Seller Central acceptance: depends on buyer availability; expect same-day to 3bd.

4) Co-sell & AWS Partner business: if you want an AWS co-sell designation (to include AWS credits or marketplace co-sell incentives), we need: a documented co-sell plan (short paragraph), primary AWS account executive name, and the forecasted ARR. That triggers a separate partner approval which typically adds 3–5 business days.

5) Pricing mechanics to confirm: for metered/usage components we recommend a blended committed spend line on the PO to simplify Marketplace acceptance. We'll flag any metering that must be billed outside Marketplace.

Deliverables I'll send after this note: a one-page checklist for procurement, a sample private-offer acceptance email, and an internal approval routing template.

If Acme can send the authorized buyer email and a PO template, we can draft the offer tomorrow and present to procurement Tuesday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Marketplace & Partner Operations
Redwood Inference
